source.title: Reconciling modern machine learning and the bias-variance trade-off
source.authors: Mikhail Belkin; Daniel J. Hsu; Si-Yuan Ma; Soumik Mandal

record.tranche_reason: The paper measures training risk across network sizes, including fully connected neural networks trained with SGD from random initialization. This bears on whether larger networks can interpolate, but it does not test the claim's convolutional architecture or full benchmark recipes.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports Random Fourier and Random ReLU feature results, but those are not gradient-based training from random initialization, so they are not rows for these versions. It cites prior work on interpolation; those cited results are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures interpolation and double descent in single-hidden-layer fully connected networks, random-feature models and tree ensembles. None tests the specified convolutional-network claim in V1 or the particular settings and mechanisms in V2–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The central conclusion is that double descent reconciles classical bias-variance behavior with successful interpolation across several model families. The authors posit an inductive-bias mechanism and discuss easier optimization in overparameterized networks; they do not establish the specific convolutional benchmark claim in V1.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SGD and random initialization in over-parameterized settings, but studies single-hidden-layer fully connected networks; CIFAR-10 is a downsampled two-class subset, not the stated convolutional benchmark setup. Weight reuse is used below the interpolation threshold in some experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Weight reuse affects the under-parameterized training procedure; without it, training loss is not monotonically decreasing, though the double-descent behavior remains discernible.

fits_no_version.finding: SGD-trained single-hidden-layer fully connected networks reach near-zero training risk in sufficiently overparameterized settings. The experiments use MNIST and a downsampled two-class CIFAR-10 subset; random initialization throughout the MNIST width sweep produces greater variability and nonmonotonic training loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sufficiently wide single-hidden-layer fully connected networks trained with SGD can interpolate the tested small image datasets, while optimization across smaller widths depends on initialization and weight reuse.

record.problems: Neural-network results are shown as plots without numerical values or error bars. CIFAR-10 uses a small, downsampled, two-class subset. The under-parameterized experiments use weight reuse in some settings, complicating comparisons across sizes.
record.rows_left_out: Random Fourier feature and Random ReLU feature curves are omitted because they do not use gradient-based training from random initialization. Other datasets and model families in the paper do not test the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: Convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, including corrupted or random labels and the stated model-size and training-recipe qualifications.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, frequencies of spurious local minima, and adding one or two student neurons.
Depth-related training degradation, identity shortcuts, and the specified plain-network and normalization-free exceptions.
Activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, training speed and trainable depth, and orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization.
Learning rates relative to the initial stability limit, transient loss growth, curvature changes, edge-of-stability dynamics and divergence.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparison with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Remove both proposed V1 verdicts. Results from a different architecture do not establish V1, and untested architecture or dataset conditions are not evidence for limits_scope. The supplied text identifies near-zero training risk qualitatively; exact plotted losses cannot be recovered from the text extraction.

versions.untested_parts: Tests single-hidden-layer fully connected networks on MNIST and a downsampled, two-class CIFAR-10 subset. Does not test convolutional networks, CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, Adam, or early stopping as a varied condition.

rows.subject: fully connected neural network with a single hidden layer
rows.size_stated: n = 960, d = 64, K = 2; network size varied by number of parameters
rows.stage_stated: trained from random initialization after the interpolation threshold
rows.operation_detail: Varied hidden units and parameter count while training with SGD; CIFAR-10 images were reduced to 8 × 8 features and the task used two classes (cat, dog).

conditions.value: subset of CIFAR-10; n = 960, d = 64, K = 2
random initialization after interpolation threshold; weight reuse before it

rows.measure: Training zero-one loss and squared loss across network sizes.
rows.uncertainty: Risks are means over five repetitions; no error bars or other uncertainty estimate stated.
rows.note: The figure plots training loss across sizes; the text says weight reuse was used before interpolation and random initialization after it. The plotted values are not stated numerically.
rows.check: The subject is a fully connected network on a downsampled, two-class CIFAR-10 subset, whereas V1 specifies convolutional networks. Its training losses cannot establish V1. The row also combines zero-one and squared loss, which should be separate measures. Figure 9 places the interpolation threshold at n·K parameters; the appendix's N ≥ n shorthand should not replace that plotted threshold.

rows.stage_stated: randomly initialized for all parameter ranges
rows.operation_detail: Varied hidden units and parameter count while training with SGD, without weight reuse.

conditions.value: random initialization for all parameter ranges

rows.measure: Training zero-one loss and squared loss across network sizes.
rows.uncertainty: Risks are means over five repetitions; no error bars or other uncertainty estimate stated.
rows.note: The text says the training loss is not monotonically decreasing in this setting, but the double descent behavior remains discernible. Plotted values are not stated numerically.
rows.check: The subject is a fully connected network on MNIST, outside V1's convolutional CIFAR-10/100 setting. Nonmonotonic training loss across widths does not test V2's teacher-student local-minimum claim or V4's comparison of activation-matched initializations. Zero-one and squared loss should be separate measures.
